name: Kai Gross
life: “I still remember planting a tree so I could grieve without explaining.” Sunday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Kai stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I planted a tree after each miscarriage. I never told the man who owns the ground.
appearance: Kai has silvery hair gathered at the nape, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Kai takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Kai uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Kai well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To get time to preserve the garden's private memorials.
family: Ethan Anand is Kai’s younger cousin. Kai chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Ethan brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The split visit*, Ethan says, “I usually get the cheerful version of our client.”
connections: Emery Rogers. The tenant's trees have an actual place to go because a neighbor offers some ground.

reactions.situation: An elderly gardener wants to move just one tree
reactions.response: Kai checks that the tree can survive the move before it is lifted.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Kai clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.
